physics_goals.quote: the most important open issue in neutrino physics: What is the absolute mass scale of neutrinos?
physics_goals.value: Directly measure (or bound) the absolute mass scale of the electron antineutrino via precision spectroscopy of tritium beta decay near its endpoint

summary.plain: A giant spectrometer in Germany that weighs neutrinos indirectly, by measuring electrons released when radioactive tritium decays. Its latest result shows the neutrino weighs no more than 0.45 electron-volts.
summary.technical: KATRIN: precision tritium beta-decay endpoint spectroscopy using a windowless gaseous tritium source and a large MAC-E (Magnetic Adiabatic Collimation with Electrostatic) filter spectrometer at KIT Campus North. The 2025 Science result, based on the first five measurement campaigns (259 measurement days, 36 million electrons), set an upper limit mν < 0.45 eV (90% CL), improving on the 2022 result of 0.8 eV by nearly a factor of two.

unique_capabilities.quote: performs precision spectroscopy of the tritium β-decay close to the kinematic endpoint
unique_capabilities.value: Model-independent, kinematic (not cosmological) measurement of the absolute neutrino mass scale via the tritium beta-decay endpoint
